summary: This article compares how countries and cultures value advanced education and how that shapes employment and economic trends in 2023. It covers cultural attitudes (South Korea, Germany, Japan), access and cost (Sweden), technology demand (India), wage premiums, entrepreneurship, practical skills (Canada), and talent migration (Australia). It concludes that advanced education drives professional success and economic development, though nations must balance it with practical skills and economic needs.
one_line: A comparative look at how national and cultural attitudes toward advanced education shape employment, wages, entrepreneurship, and talent migration in 2023.
key_facts: The International Institute for Educational Advancement (IIEA) released a study on September 5, 2023 showing societies place varying importance on advanced education.
Dr. Min-Jun Kim of Seoul said that in 2023 South Korea saw 93% of its high school graduates transition to universities, many pursuing STEM degrees.

Ottmar Heinrich, a training coordinator from Munich, explained on September 12, 2023 that Germany's dual education system merges education with apprenticeships and often leads to long-term employment with the training company.
In Sweden there are no tuition fees for EU/EEA students, and non-EU international students face relatively modest fees; labor economist Dr. Eva Jansson commented on this on September 20, 2023.
Technology educator Priya Gupta said on September 30, 2023 that India saw a 15% increase in enrolment for online advanced degree programs in AI, data science, and machine learning in 2023.
An Economic Policy Research Center report released October 10, 2023 found individuals with advanced degrees earn on average 35% more than those with only secondary education.
Sociologist Maya Tanaka of Tokyo said on November 1, 2023 that in Japan basic entry-level positions now often require a university degree as a minimum.
Canada values a mix of university education and college diplomas or certificates; workforce analyst James Beckett stated this on November 15, 2023.
Startup advisor Jessica Nguyen of Silicon Valley said on December 2, 2023 that an MBA offers entrepreneurs in-depth business knowledge and a vital network.

Immigration expert Hugh Mitchell said on December 20, 2023 that Australia's policy allowing international students to work after graduation has retained talent, benefiting technology sectors and research institutions.
The article argues the wage premium varies across economies and may be higher where fewer people hold degrees.
The article notes a growing debate that not all roles require a degree and that skills can be learned on the job or through vocational training.
